penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: The primary users are individual event organizers and small community managers — consumer/prosumer segment that expects free Google add-ons and whose aggregate revenue would require hundreds or thousands of paying users to be meaningful.

rationale: Event organizers using Google Forms have a real, recurring duplicate-booking problem, and the technical build is genuinely easy — Claude + Apps Script logic + a simple notification layer is achievable in days. But the buyers are individual consumers and community managers who expect free Google Workspace tooling; there is no demonstrated willingness to pay (3) and buyer clarity is low (3) — this is a 'everyone' audience without budget authority. After the b2c-scale penalty, total is 3.6. The combination of weak commercial signal and a market that expects free tools makes this a drop.
solution_plan: Not commercially viable as a micro-service. The technical problem is easy to solve (a Google Apps Script runs the duplicate check and sends an email alert), but the people who need it expect free solutions — the Google Workspace Marketplace is full of free add-ons, and community event managers don't have software budgets. Even at $5/month, converting enough users to meaningful revenue would require thousands of customers. The factory's time is better spent on B2B buyers with real budgets. Drop.
notes: Fails willingness_to_pay (3 < 5) and buyer_clarity (3 < 6) build gates. Total after penalty is 3.6, below validate threshold.
